design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (homeowner_claims_and_replacement), revision 5

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [6, 5, 4]. Assignment: company-elected offer (homeplan_ext_company_elected_cash_offer) 6, haul-away allowance (homeplan_ext_haul_away_on_completed_replacement) 5, acceptance (homeplan_ext_company_cash_acceptance) 4.

[Revision 5 log] The homeplan render and the round-4 audit raised source-quotation and coverage points, none of which moves a figure: (a) the acceptance's compute_basis for the outage item now quotes the rule verbatim ('had stood on the date of the accepted offer'; O-r4-1); (b) the haul-away rule now states that no haul-away allowance is owed or booked on a tier whose haul_away_allowance is 0.00, so the rule never asks the allowance tool for a 0.00 amount, and the offer's prerequisite sentence and its condition now wait on the haul-away only for a replacement on a tier that pays one — the Platinum contract here pays 150.00, so the gate and both writes are unchanged; (c) every replaced_by now restates the parts of its retired base clause that stay in force — the shared item cap, the aggregate counting of every payment, the remaining item and aggregate benefits (including the item half on the haul-away policy, which no allowance enters), the offer's benefit limits and rounding, the acceptance's start from the accepted offer amount and its settlement_basis, and the fees that are still not refunded.

[Revision 4 log] Policy audit round 3 found R3-F1: the network-miss credit's repeat tier rested on line-plan dispatches made to plumbing-trade contractors, which the line-plan charter never produces (lineplan_evt_dispatch sends a line request to a utility_line contractor), and its stated reason was a failure of 'the plumbing network'. It also recorded O-r3-2 (a missed contact on the household's own homeowner-contract requests should count first) and O-r3-3 (the outage credit accrued up to the acceptance date, so an offer held open kept accruing days that are no longer Bridgewell's delay). Changes: (a) the line plan's May request is now a slow-draining kitchen drain line (interior_drain_line, routine, nothing leaking), assigned under the line-plan charter to the preferred utility_line contractor serving 78745 (Hill Country Line Services), re-dispatched to the standard one (Pecan Street Utility Lines) on May 15 after the 48-hour window was missed, determined covered on the homeowner side, repaired with section repair 1260516318 (240.00, inside the 3000.00 interior plumbing occurrence cap) and completed on May 19; the two line contractors were added to the world and are read; (b) the repeat tier's reason is now a repeat failure of Bridgewell's contractor network for the household, and it counts an earlier missed-contact re-dispatch on another of the household's homeowner-contract requests first, then one on a request under a Bridgewell line plan the customer holds; this household has none of the former, so the line plan still decides the tier; (c) the outage days now run to the date of the accepted offer, not to the acceptance date; on this world the offer and the acceptance fall on the same day, so no figure moves.

[Revision 3 log] Policy audit round 2 found: R2-F1 (the supply-line coordination ladder had an unreachable middle tier, since every line plan covering interior supply lines carries a 3000.00 limit, and its tiers were one coordination formula; reconnecting a new unit is installation, not a line failure), R2-F2 (the expansion-tank ladder paid nothing to a customer with no rider, so it turned on holding a rider rather than on the water source), R2-F3 (no cross-difficulty factor survived), and the observations O-r2-1 (the gate sentence said 'the Bridgewell replacement most recently completed' while the condition and compute read the most recent completion report), O-r2-2 (the base remaining-benefit sentence was not named), O-r2-4 (code, disposal and permit additions inside cash against the base sentence 'Allowances are never paid on a cash-in-lieu settlement'), O-r2-5 (the network-miss credit and the visit-fee return both rested on the same missed-contact re-dispatch) and O-r2-6 (the acceptance paid more than the accepted offer, adding disposal and permits the offer could have stated). Changes: (a) both line-plan and rider ladders are gone; the offer now carries a supply reconnection charge and an outside-installer labor gap decided by the item, and the cross-difficulty factor is the network-miss credit, whose repeat tier applies when a request under the customer's Bridgewell line plan was also re-dispatched after a missed contact window within the twelve months before today; the world gained the May 12 kitchen-sink supply-line request that Barton Creek Plumbing Co. missed and Lone Star Water Heater Pros repaired (revision 4 replaced that out-of-charter plumbing dispatch with the line plan's own utility_line route), and lost the rider, which no rule reads any more; (b) the gate sentence, the edge condition and the haul-away rule now all speak of the most recent completion report on the contract, when it closes a Bridgewell replacement; (c) every policy names the base remaining-benefit sentence in its scoped overwrite; (d) the offer declares a scoped overwrite of the allowance-on-cash sentence for its code-compliance, disposal and permit additions and books no allowance row; (e) everything the homeowner must pay to have the like unit installed — re-quoted unit, reconnection, outside labor, drain pan, disposal, permit — is now in the offer, so the offer states the cash in place of the replacement; the acceptance pays that amount as offered and settles with it only the credits owed for Bridgewell's own service failures on the recall (outage days, the visit fee of the failed installation, the early-failure credit and the network-miss credit), which close with the claim; (f) the visit-fee return now turns on whether the recall names an earlier Bridgewell replacement or repair, so the missed-contact re-dispatch feeds the network-miss credit alone.

[Scope snapshot] Task 0 claims the stalled-repair replacement (authorize_stalled_repair_replacement_b6f80e12) and the customer-elected cash (elect_cash_in_place_of_replacement_7cf483ad). Claimed here: homeplan_ext_haul_away_on_completed_replacement (book_supplemental_allowance_cce1a240, agent), homeplan_ext_company_elected_cash_offer (issue_company_cash_offer_eabc2067, agent), homeplan_ext_company_cash_acceptance (accept_company_cash_offer_2503240a, user). The two tasks cover all five extended policies; no policy or tool is shared.

[Why this is a good test] The customer only asks to be paid so she can hire her own plumber. The agent must see from the network list that no plumber can install (company-elected, which also excludes task 0's customer-elected route), read in the offer rule that an offer is issued only once the most recent completion report, when it closes a Bridgewell replacement on a tier that pays a haul-away allowance, has that replacement's haul-away allowance, find that the July water heater installation has none, book it (five rules), issue the offer (six rules), and hand the customer the acceptance, whose payment applies four more rules — one of them read from the line plan's claim history.

[Problem-tree card] root homeplan_ext_company_cash_acceptance. Edge 1: homeplan_ext_company_cash_acceptance <- homeplan_ext_company_elected_cash_offer, value_input, gate accepted_offer_amount, form state, sentence (acceptance rule): "The cash paid on accepting a company-elected settlement is not fixed until an unexpired company-elected cash-in-lieu offer stands on the service request." — connective "not ... until", a record-visible state (an unexpired company-elected offer on the request), no tool/id/code token, hard strength. Only the offer tool writes offers. Unmet: no cash-in-lieu row of any kind on the contract at frozen_time. Edge 2: homeplan_ext_company_elected_cash_offer <- homeplan_ext_haul_away_on_completed_replacement, state_gate, gate homeplan_claim_events.allowance_type, form state, sentence (offer rule): "A company-elected cash-in-lieu offer is issued only once the most recent completion report on the contract, when it closes a Bridgewell replacement on a tier that pays a haul-away allowance, has that replacement's haul-away allowance on the records." — connective "only once", record-visible state, hard strength. Only the supplemental-allowance tool, the haul-away policy's target, writes allowances. Unmet: the 2026-07-10 completion report closes replacement 1260629471, whose request carries no allowance (the only allowance on the contract is the 2025 garbage disposal haul-away). value_input edges 1 >= max(2-1, 1). Topological order: haul-away (step 12), offer (step 14), acceptance (step 16). Deletion sensitivity: without the offer the acceptance cannot be evaluated at all, because with no company-elected offer on the request there is no accepted offer amount to start from; without the allowance the offer stays 1472.6 but the allowance row is missing from the terminal state.

[Base-invariant card] Haul-away write: live_authorization_on_request — 1260629471 is not reversed (the only reversal on the contract, of 2025-09-17, takes back duplicate authorization 1250916513 on the garbage disposal request); one_allowance_per_type_per_request — no allowance on the June 26 request; benefit_caps policy_scope. Offer write: homeplan_evt_cash_in_lieu has no gate on issuing an offer; the company-elected ground is shown by the contractor records. Acceptance write: one_cash_settlement_per_request — no cash on the recall; the offer is accepted on its offer date, inside cash_in_lieu_offer_validity_days (the gate scripts treat that time gate as retired because task 0's customer-elected overwrite retires it for customer-elected settlements; for this company-elected acceptance it still holds: offer 2026-10-15, expiry 2026-11-14, accepted 2026-10-15). The standing authorization is reversed in full; it has no completion report.

[Business-object card] Haul-away: the June 26 request 9e96b3af-5c78-4ba2-8094-3ef7faae519b, replacement 1260629471, completion 2026-07-10. Offer and acceptance: the August 24 recall 62e1df50-c7ff-4349-a724-91124a382a41, standing authorization 1260828733 (980.00). Water heater payments dated after 2025-10-15: 1260629471 980.00 and 1260828733 980.00 (1960.00), the latter taken back out as if reversed -> 2020.00 remaining of the 3000.00 cap. The 2025 garbage disposal replacement (330.00), its reversed duplicate authorization and its 42.00 haul-away are older than twelve months and only serve as the near-miss for the gate. The line plan's 240.00 repair is a line-plan benefit and counts toward no homeplan limit.

[Factor card — haul-away, 5] removed_equipment_class (parameter) water heater -> 45.00 (baseline 30.00 -> 76.7); carry_out_ladder (parameter, multi-source: dwelling type x request trade) townhome + plumbing -> 12.00 (baseline -> 79.7); unit_size_ladder (parameter) contracted cost 980.00 -> 8.00 (baseline -> 83.7); after_hours_removal_ladder (parameter) after-hours routine installation visit -> 20.00 (baseline -> 71.7); late_booking_day_count (method) 97 days -> 0.10 per day beyond 30 = 6.70 (baseline none -> 85.0). Whole baseline 30.0; gold 91.7.

[Factor card — offer, 6] offer_requote_ladder 48 days -> 0.02 (baseline -> 1453.0); supply_reconnection_ladder water heater -> 95.00 (baseline -> 1377.6); outside_installer_method (method) licensed trade -> 10% of the recorded 980.00 = 98.00, against a flat delivery gap for an appliance (baseline none -> 1374.6); attached_dwelling_code_pan (multi-source) water heater in a townhome -> 85.00 (baseline -> 1387.6); failed_unit_disposal water heater -> 45.00 (baseline -> 1427.6); owner_permit_ladder water heater -> 1 x 150.00 (baseline -> 1322.6). Whole baseline 980.0; gold 1472.6.

[Factor card — acceptance, 4] outage_day_count (method) water heater, 52 days up to the offer date -> 156.00 (baseline -> 1817.6); recall_fee_return_ladder (multi-source: recall x the earlier authorization it names) earlier work was a Bridgewell replacement -> the full 125.00 June fee (baseline -> 1848.6); early_failure_method (method) failure 45 days after the July installation -> flat 100.00 goodwill rather than the 25% installation share reserved for failures within 30 days (baseline none -> 1873.6); network_miss_ladder (multi-source, cross-difficulty lineplan) a missed contact on the recall after one on the line plan in May, with none on the household's other homeowner-contract requests -> repeat credit 120.00 (baseline -> 1853.6). Whole baseline 1472.6; gold 1973.6.

[Rows and why they exist] Customer; Platinum townhome contract (tier, dwelling, billing, term); line plan LP1 with its May 12 interior drain-line request, two assignments (Hill Country Line Services missed the contact window, Pecan Street Utility Lines was re-dispatched), covered determination, repair authorization and completion (the cross-difficulty repeat-miss evidence); the two utility_line contractors that line plan's assignments name; three plumbing contractors (two suspended serving 78745, one outside the ZIP as near-miss); the 2025 garbage disposal replacement with its haul-away (near-miss for the gate, previous term and older than twelve months) and a duplicate authorization issued for it the same day and reversed the next day (the record the live-authorization gate reads; net zero and older than twelve months); the June water heater request, replacement and completion (haul-away object, earlier work named by the recall, its 125.00 fee); the August recall with its two assignments, determination and standing replacement; two annual premiums with payments and two visit fees. No automatic clause fires beyond the ones this task carries: premiums are paid, the renewal notice is not yet due, no other allowance or offer is owed.

[Persona design] Marisol volunteers the surface goal (be paid so she can hire her own plumber), the history the records hold (July installation, leak on August 24th, installer never called back, a second company came, told it would be replaced, nobody installed it) and her hard preference (no more waiting). She volunteers the leak date; her identity details and the installation date come only when asked. She never mentions the May kitchen-drain request. Passive branches: lets the agent settle account matters first, refuses another plumber search, runs the handed-over acceptance with the agent's details, closes on confirmation. No figure, no haul-away and no offer is mentioned.

[Most likely mistakes] (1) Taking the customer-elected route because the customer asks for money. (2) Issuing the offer without first booking the haul-away owed for the July installation (the 2025 disposal haul-away does not satisfy the gate). (3) Leaving the self-installation costs out of the offer or adding them again at acceptance. (4) Paying the single-miss credit because the line plan's claim history was never read. (5) Applying the 25% installation share although the failure came after 30 days. (6) Counting the outage from the authorization date (48 days) instead of the request date (52), or past the offer date.

[Standard solution] locate -> verify -> read contract, requests, claim history, billing, plumbing contractors, line plans, the line plan's requests and claim history, the line contractors -> supplemental allowance (9e96b3af-5c78-4ba2-8094-3ef7faae519b, haul_away, 85.0, 91.7) -> company-elected offer (62e1df50-c7ff-4349-a724-91124a382a41, water_heater, 999.6, 1472.6, 2026-11-14) -> hand over the acceptance (62e1df50-c7ff-4349-a724-91124a382a41, water_heater, 1260828733, 980.00, 1973.6).

[Verification run] sim.py on the replayed world: haul-away 91.7 (baseline 30.0, factors [('removed_equipment_class', 76.7), ('carry_out_ladder', 79.7), ('unit_size_ladder', 83.7), ('after_hours_removal_ladder', 71.7), ('late_booking_day_count', 85.0)]); offer after step 12 1472.6 (baseline 980.0, factors [('offer_requote_ladder', 1453.0), ('supply_reconnection_ladder', 1377.6), ('outside_installer_method', 1374.6), ('attached_dwelling_code_pan', 1387.6), ('failed_unit_disposal', 1427.6), ('owner_permit_ladder', 1322.6)]; without step 12 1472.6); acceptance after step 14 1973.6 (baseline 1472.6, factors [('outage_day_count', 1817.6), ('recall_fee_return_ladder', 1848.6), ('early_failure_method', 1873.6), ('network_miss_ladder', 1853.6)]); without step 14 the acceptance cannot be evaluated at all, because with no company-elected offer on the request there is no accepted offer amount to start from.

[Closure] homeplan_ext_haul_away_on_completed_replacement -> book_supplemental_allowance_cce1a240 -> computations[0] step 12 amount; homeplan_ext_company_elected_cash_offer -> issue_company_cash_offer_eabc2067 -> computations[1] step 14 amount; homeplan_ext_company_cash_acceptance -> accept_company_cash_offer_2503240a -> computations[2] step 16 payment_amount. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies.

[Gate run] check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding, check_cross_fire: OK per task and difficulty-wide; check_traceability: the only misses are the three unlock tool names, which become reachable once the KB is rendered.
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Vandersteen-Achebe, a hospital pharmacist who owns a townhome at 1907 Calloway Bend, Unit 4 in Austin and has had a Bridgewell homeowner plan on it since spring 2024. You are short on patience and get to the point. Bridgewell put in a new water heater for you in July. On August 24th that new water heater started leaking at the bottom of the tank and you had to shut the cold water valve. The plumber who installed it never called you back, a second plumbing company came out a couple of days later, and you were told Bridgewell would replace the water heater. Since then nobody has come to install it, the plumbing companies stop answering, and you have been heating water on the stove for weeks. You open by saying all of this briefly and asking Bridgewell to pay you the money so you can hire your own plumber, because you are done waiting.

When the agent asks who you are you give your full name, Marisol Vandersteen-Achebe. To confirm your identity you give the phone number on the account, 5125550113, and your ZIP code, 78745; if one more detail is needed you give your email, marisol.vandersteen.achebe@kestrelpost.net. You do not have any contract or claim numbers handy and you say the plan is under your name at the Calloway Bend address. If the agent asks, the new water heater started leaking on August 24th and it was installed around July 10th.

If the agent says Bridgewell has to take care of something on your account before the money can be offered, you tell them to go ahead. If the agent offers to keep looking for another plumber instead, you say no, you want the money. When the agent tells you how much you will be paid and hands you the step to accept it, you carry it out with exactly the details the agent gives you and read back the confirmation. If the agent only states a figure without giving you a way to accept it, you ask how you accept. Once the agent confirms the payment is recorded, you thank them and hang up.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain: haul-away allowance -> company-elected offer -> acceptance. The offer policy's own rule pins the first link ('A company-elected cash-in-lieu offer is issued only once the most recent completion report on the contract, when it closes a Bridgewell replacement on a tier that pays a haul-away allowance, has that replacement's haul-away allowance on the records.'), and the acceptance rule pins the second ('The cash paid on accepting a company-elected settlement is not fixed until an unexpired company-elected cash-in-lieu offer stands on the service request.'). The offer amount is the same whether or not the allowance is booked first (1472.6 either way, because the remaining aggregate benefit does not bind), so that gate only orders the writes; the acceptance cannot precede the offer because it starts from the offer's amount.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 14 leaves no company-elected offer on the recall: the acceptance computation cannot be evaluated at all, because with no company-elected offer on the request there is no accepted offer amount to start from; the terminal state also lacks the offer row. With the offer, the payment is 1973.6.

Skipping step 12 leaves the July water heater replacement without its haul-away allowance: the terminal state lacks the 91.7 allowance row and the offer is issued while its gate is unmet (its amount stays 1472.6); state_gate edge.
